issues.message: index.js still contains console.log("PASSWORD:", password) inside login() — plaintext credentials get written to logs/stdout. This line is untouched context in the diff, so it's a pre-existing issue, but this PR modifies the very function it's in and adds no fix; it should be removed or replaced with redacted logging.

In ci-review.yml, `git diff origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD > pr.diff || touch pr.diff` swallows any failure (e.g. base-ref fetch failure) into an empty pr.diff. The new 'if [ ! -s pr.diff ]' guard then writes `{"passed": true, "issues": []}` and the workflow exits 0. This means any failure in producing the diff — not just a genuinely empty PR — silently bypasses the AI review gate and reports a pass, defeating the purpose of the security gate.

pr.diff and review.json (CI-generated artifacts) are being committed into the repository as tracked files. These are ephemeral outputs of the workflow and shouldn't be checked in — they add noise, can go stale, and in this case the committed pr.diff even embeds an older nested diff of the same workflow file, which is confusing.

ci-review.yml interpolates `${{ github.base_ref }}` directly into the `run:` shell script rather than passing it through an `env:` variable. This is a known GitHub Actions script-injection anti-pattern; base_ref is lower-risk than head_ref/title but the safer pattern is still to pass untrusted/context values via env and reference them as shell variables.
